answer: A nebula of agents can resist sybils with a quartz-anchored audit trail: every completed job is sealed to one identity and cannot be transferred, and independent auditors wander through old jobs at random and re-run them. A clone starts with no history, so an attacker wanting 200 voting identities must genuinely complete 40 verified jobs per clone, 8000 jobs in total, spending about 40000 hours of compute and locking 10000 coins as deposits. One copied or faked job burns that clone's whole 50-coin deposit, so mass cloning costs real work instead of cheap copies.
